slo_title: Illustrate control structures and step-by-step execution in procedural languages

mcq.q: What is the main focus of the imperative programming paradigm?

options.A: a) What the result should be
options.B: b) How to achieve the result through instructions

mcq.answer_text: b) How to achieve the result through instructions

mcq.q: int x = 5; if (x > 3) { System.out.print("Hello"); } else { System.out.print("Bye"); }
Which one is a key characteristic of procedural programming?

options.A: a) Uses objects and classes exclusively
options.B: b) Focuses on facts and rules
options.C: c) Code is organized into reusable procedures/functions

mcq.answer_text: c) Code is organized into reusable procedures/functions

mcq.q: Which of the following correctly describes the execution of procedural code in Java?**

options.B: b) Code is compiled but not executed
options.C: c) Code is executed step-by-step from top to bottom
options.D: d) Only class declarations are executed

mcq.answer_text: c) Code is executed step-by-step from top to bottom

sq.q: A vehicle management application includes categories like cars, trucks, and motorcycles. What object-oriented features are most suitable for this system?
answer: Inheritance allows shared vehicle attributes, encapsulation manages private data such as engine details, and polymorphism enables common interfaces for all vehicle types, enhancing scalability.

sq.q: An application has repetitive code across several classes for logging activities. How can object-oriented design address this issue?
answer: Abstracting shared logic into a superclass or utility class promotes code reuse and simplifies updates by centralizing common behavior.

lq.q: Design a library management system using object-oriented programming principles. Demonstrate how classes , inheritance , and encapsulation can be applied to model books, members, and librarians.
answer: class Book { private String title; private String author; private boolean isAvailable; public Book(String title, String author) { this.title = title; this.author = author; this.isAvailable = true; } public boolean isAvailable() { return isAvailable; } public void borrowBook() { isAvailable = false; } public void returnBook() { isAvailable = true; } } class User { protected String name; protected String userId; } class Member extends User { private List<Book> borrowedBooks = new ArrayList<>(); public void borrow(Book b) { if (b.isAvailable()) { borrowedBooks.add(b); b.borrowBook(); } } } class Librarian extends User { public void addBook(List<Book> library, Book b) { library.add(b); } }
class Book { private String title; private String author; private boolean isAvailable;
public Book(String title, String author) { this.title = title; this.author = author; this.isAvailable = true; }
public boolean isAvailable() { return isAvailable; } public void borrowBook() { isAvailable = false; } public void returnBook() { isAvailable = true; } }

class Member extends User { private List<Book> borrowedBooks = new ArrayList<>();
public void borrow(Book b) { if (b.isAvailable()) { borrowedBooks.add(b); b.borrowBook(); } } }
class Librarian extends User { public void addBook(List<Book> library, Book b) { library.add(b); } }
